timeline.event: Rostekhnadzor orders Nornickel to clean tank surfaces and restore anticorrosion coating by 2015
Rostekhnadzor deadline for non-destructive inspection of tank bottoms - not completed by Nornickel
Fuel storage Tank 5 at Nornickel CHPP-3 (Norilsk-Taimyr Energy) collapses, releasing 17,500-21,000 tonnes of diesel into Daldykan and Ambarnaya rivers
Incident remains unreported for two days while company attempts containment
Russian government agencies learn of spill; Investigative Committee launches criminal investigation
Spill reaches Lake Pyasino, threatening Pyasina River and Arctic Ocean
Putin holds televised meeting, criticizes local authorities and questions NTEK head Sergei Lipin about delayed reporting
President Putin declares federal state of emergency; publicly criticizes Vladimir Potanin for safety failures
Head of CHPP-3 boiler-turbine workshop placed in pretrial detention on charges of environmental violations and negligence
Rosprirodnadzor employee Vasily Ryabinin quits and goes public as whistleblower after being told to stop investigating
Oleg Deripaska (Rusal, 28% stake) publicly calls for management changes at Nornickel, citing spill as evidence of governance failures
Prosecutor General orders safety checks at all dangerous installations built on permafrost in Russian Arctic
Greenpeace Russia compares potential environmental impact to Exxon Valdez spill
Rosprirodnadzor presents claim for 148 billion rubles in environmental damages
Shareholder conflict intensifies: Potanin (Interros, 35%) vs Deripaska (Rusal, 28%) over corporate governance and dividend policy
Nornickel disputes the damage assessment, challenges fine in court
Continued shareholder tensions: Rusal pushes for board changes and governance reforms
Russian court orders Nornickel to pay record fine of 146 billion rubles ($2 billion) for environmental damage
Nornickel begins cleanup operations, estimated cost 100 billion rubles, timeline 5-10 years
One year anniversary: Environmental monitoring continues, corporate governance reforms partially implemented

narrative_trajectory.N0_normal: 2014-2020 (pre-spill) - Routine industrial operations, ignored safety warnings from regulators
narrative_trajectory.N1_weak_problematization: May 29-31, 2020 - Initial incident, delayed reporting, internal containment attempts
narrative_trajectory.N2_sustained_problematization: June 1-3, 2020 - Public discovery, criminal investigation, spill spreads
narrative_trajectory.N3_personalization: June 3-10, 2020 - Putin criticizes Potanin personally, arrests of plant managers, Deripaska attacks Potanin governance
narrative_trajectory.N4_systemic_crisis: June-December 2020 - Broad questions about Arctic infrastructure, corporate governance, shareholder conflict, environmental policy
narrative_trajectory.N5_resolution: February 2021 onward - Record fine imposed, cleanup begins, governance reforms implemented

tone_shift_hypothesis: Dramatic shift from industrial accident to national crisis within 5 days. Putin's personal criticism of Potanin transformed narrative from environmental disaster to corporate governance failure. Shareholder conflict added layer of elite infighting. Russian media: initial restraint, then extensive coverage after Putin's statement. International media: environmental catastrophe framing, Arctic climate implications.
collection_recommendation: Focus on May 29, 2020 - February 2021. Russian sources: 60-70%. Priority: federal news agencies (TASS, RIA, Interfax), business press (RBC, Kommersant, Vedomosti), international wire services. Key events: June 3-4 (Putin statements), June 10 (Deripaska intervention), February 5, 2021 (court fine). Monitor shareholder communications from both Interros and Rusal.
